rules.text: Two nights or more is kinder; a suggestion, never a reason to pad
No move over 90 minutes with the New Year crowds (out of Tokyo and Kansai 26–30 Dec, back 2–4 Jan); 31 Dec and 1 Jan are calm; moves against the flow get a booking note
Flag any activity planned on a date its place is closed (closures and closed_weekdays)
Stays must cover 20 Dec to 9 Jan without gaps
Arrange New Year's Eve dinner ahead: most restaurants close (a ryokan, a booked restaurant or cooking in)
Show effort_for_her and avoid_for_her on every planned item
No day over about 4 hours door to door
No moves on consecutive days, and no more than three in any week
No more nights than a place can fill; a named day trip (Shirakawa-go from Kanazawa, the ski or Obuse day from Yudanaka) earns one more; hubs count their easy day trips
The night of 8 Jan near Haneda; no more than 2 nights in Tokyo at the end unless the first Tokyo stay was short
Every night within about 30 minutes of obstetric care; 29 Dec – 3 Jan near a perinatal centre; missing data shows as not checked
Long stays in places Pedro and Fernanda already know should be for the first-timers

deadlines.item: Book now: Shibu Onsen (or Yudanaka) for 24–27 Dec, for 7, with beds, a lift and a private bath (Kokuya, Kanaguya, Biyunoyado); only Shibu's inn guests get the key to its nine baths. Book only through official channels; Kanaguya warns of fake emails

Book now: Kyoto, 30 Dec – 5 Jan, for 7, on the flat streets just west of Yasaka Shrine (Gion-Shijo / Kawaramachi), not up in the Higashiyama lanes, which close to cars on New Year's Eve. A townhouse with a full lodging licence (a home-share in a residential zone cannot take guests over New Year; ask about ground-floor beds, stairs and heating), or a ryokan for 30–31 Dec plus a second base for 1–5 Jan. Ask it to accept the big cases on 30 Dec
Book now: Kanazawa 27–30 Dec, for 7, ideally an apartment with a washing machine
Check the nearest obstetric emergency hospital for Kawaguchiko, then book the lake (or Hakone) for 5–7 Jan, for 7
Agree the route as a family: New Year's Eve at Yasaka Shrine or a calm ryokan dinner, Kawaguchiko or Hakone, a van or the bus to Shirakawa-go, and whether Takayama comes back
Ghibli Museum tickets for December dates go on sale
Book a van with a driver for Mon 28 Dec, Kanazawa – Shirakawa-go – Kanazawa (about ¥80,000–100,000 for the day), or plan on the Nohi bus
10:00 JST: reserve shinkansen seats Tokyo → Nagano for 24 Dec. Every later leg goes on sale one month ahead at 10:00 JST
10:00 JST: reserve the Kagayaki Nagano → Kanazawa for 27 Dec, Green Car. The train starts in Tokyo on a busy day, so seats for 7 may go fast
Only if there is no van: book the Nohi bus Kanazawa → Shirakawa-go and back for 28 Dec (8:40 out). Seven seats together are not guaranteed
10:00 JST: reserve the 30 Dec trains, Hokuriku shinkansen Kanazawa → Tsuruga and the Thunderbird to Kyoto, Green Car
14:00 JST, optional: Chion-in bell viewing tickets for New Year's Eve (¥3,000 in 2025, sold out online by 9 Dec)
10:00 JST: reserve the shinkansen Kyoto → Mishima for 5 Jan (or Kyoto → Odawara for Hakone)
Sumo January tournament tickets on sale, if extending to 10 Jan
10:00 JST: reserve the Fuji Excursion Kawaguchiko → Shinjuku for 7 Jan; it sells out weeks ahead
Book the airport transfer to Haneda for Sat 9 Jan
Ghibli Museum tickets for January dates go on sale
Mid-December: recheck the New Year's Eve bell times, the Okera fire times, Obuse's holiday hours, the Shiga Kogen opening date and the trains' year-end notices

places.name: Mishima Skywalk

places.name: Nirayama reverberatory furnace

places.name: Hokoku-ji bamboo garden

places.hours: 9:00–16:00; closed 29 Dec–3 Jan

places.name: Enoshima

places.name: Enoshima Aquarium (Enosui)

places.hours: Open every day; New Year hours usually 9:00–17:00

places.name: Sankeien garden, Yokohama

places.name: Shichirigahama beach

places.name: Zuigan-ji

places.name: Yamadera (Risshaku-ji)
